description: List what we tried to POST and what your server answered, newest first. Look here when an event never arrived. Narrow it with `status` (pending, delivered, failed) and with `type`, an event type. A cursor works only with the filters it came from. A row whose `eventType` is `webhook.test` is a test from `test_webhook`: it has no event or subject, is never retryable, and is not in `failed`. A failed attempt says why in `errorCode` (timeout, redirect, status, network, unreachable, url_invalid, endpoint_off, test_lost), with the seconds waited or the socket's error in `errorDetail`, and in `error` as one English sentence. `subject` names the row the event was about: its `kind` (send, mailbox, message, campaign, handoff, suppression, email_check_run, workspace, mail_domain, tracking_domain) and its `id`, plus `threadId` on a message. It is null once the event is no longer kept (24 hours), and it never says the row is still there. `failed` counts the deliveries that failed in the 30 days the list keeps, whatever the filters. It stops at 1000, which means that many or more. A signed-in owner can call this, or an API key with both setup and read permission.

cursor.description: Where the last page stopped: the nextCursor of the answer before. Use it with the same filters it came with. Left out, the list starts at the beginning.

limit.description: How many to return in one page, 1 to 200. Left out, the server picks.

status.description: Only deliveries in these states. In a URL, repeat the parameter: ?status=failed&status=pending.

type.description: Only deliveries of these event types. In a URL, repeat the parameter: ?type=send.sent&type=send.failed.

name: list_webhook_deliveries
title: List webhook deliveries
